symptom: `check -p` passed a fully qualified page attribute path (`"Mod"."BomLine_Part"/"Mod"."Product"/"Sku"`, `"Mod"."Product"/System.changedBy/System.User/Name`) without a word while exec silently stored the short form; and `"Mod"."Product"/"Sku"` (leading entity, then the attribute) passed check and exec and was written unbound — mxbuild 11.16.0 CE0402 on a text param, CE7005 on a text box, "An attribute is required" on a Data grid 2 column.
cause: resolveAssociationPathFrom drops a leading context-entity step only when len(segs) > 2, so the two-segment form fell back to the flat writer. check never asked exec's resolver about any page path; and the scope walk marks a pluggable data widget's children unresolved, so grid columns and gallery items were never judged at all.
fix: attributeScopeValidator.checkQualifiedAttributePaths runs exec's own resolver on every qualified path (input/column Attribute, ContentParams/CaptionParams, rooted at a parameter too) and finds the short form by dropping each qualified segment whose absence leaves the identical final attribute and steps — MDL-ATTRPATH01 warning; the two-segment leading-entity form is refused with the bare attribute — MDL-ATTRPATH02. checkDataWidgetItemPaths judges grid columns and gallery content against the datasource entity.
insight: Derive the 'what will be stored' message by asking the write path's resolver (drop a segment, compare the resolution) instead of re-encoding its normalisation rules — a copy is how check and exec drifted. Probe with describe + bson dump per shape before deciding which side is right: every 3+ segment shape normalised and built clean (mx check 0 errors, snippet/System.changedBy included), only the 2-segment form did not. Also found, not fixed: ALTER PAGE SET attribute on a built-in input writes an association path verbatim (short form: AttributeRef null), and a pluggable widget's primary attribute: resolves `Assoc/Attr` flat.
test: mdl/executor/check_qualified_attribute_path_pedapp_test.go TestCheckQualifiedAttributePath_* (controls: short forms and a microflow $X/Mod.Assoc/Mod.Entity/Attr say nothing)
